title: Vitess: mysqld-wire cert-rotate (online ALTER INSTANCE RELOAD TLS, no reparent)
description: cert-rotate vitess (GAP #12, v0.8.9) now rotates the tablet's mysqld-WIRE cert too (:3306 -- replication + vt_dba + vtgate->mysqld), not just the vttablet gRPC cert. Each node's vault-agent is forced to re-issue a fresh, DURABLE leaf (rm bundle.pem -> restart agent -> post-render split; pkiCert otherwise reuses its cached leaf and reverts a direct write -- a pre-existing durability bug this fix also closes), then the tablet's mysqld reloads the wire cert ONLINE via ALTER INSTANCE RELOAD TLS (Percona 8.4 -- no restart, NO reparent, the PRIMARY is never demoted). Live-verified 2026-07-07.

prerequisites.smokeGate: nexus health vitess green (both shards 1 PRIMARY + 2 REPLICA); nodes on the current Vault root

observe.what: record which tablet is each shard's PRIMARY (e.g. shard1-tablet-2, shard2-tablet-1) -- to confirm NO reparent after the rotation
all 12 nodes rotate GREEN with fresh serials and no error -- a tablet row with no error means its mysqld `ALTER INSTANCE RELOAD TLS` succeeded (it only succeeds if the new cert/key/ca load)

observe.where: ssh nexusadmin@<shard-primary-ip> 'sudo openssl x509 -in /etc/nexus-vitess/tls/server-cert.pem -noout -serial; echo | sudo openssl s_client -starttls mysql -connect 127.0.0.1:3306 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -serial'
observe.what: the on-disk serial CHANGED and PERSISTS, and mysqld SERVES that same new serial -- the wire cert was reloaded online + durably (agent holds the new leaf)
the shard PRIMARIES are UNCHANGED from step 1 -- no reparent happened; `nexus health vitess` stays green (both shards 1 PRIMARY + 2 REPLICA, operator-auth via vtgate->mysqld mTLS)

whatProves: The tablet's mysqld-wire cert rotates as a real, in-CLI operation: the leaf is re-issued durably (force-rerender, no silent revert) and mysqld reloads it ONLINE via ALTER INSTANCE RELOAD TLS -- with no mysqld restart, no PlannedReparentShard, and no change of primary. Replication + vt_dba + vtgate->mysqld all keep working on the new cert.
